svg.title: Pulsus Dash — Infra view, Group by: workload — Kubernetes workloads of prod-eu-1 in 3D (INC-2041)
svg.desc: Perspective 3D Workload arrangement of the Kubernetes cluster prod-eu-1 (Infra view, ⌥4, Group by: workload). Namespaces are districts on a glass cluster plateau: payments, checkout, catalog, data and kube-system. Each Deployment is a tower of stacked replica blocks, one block per pod. The checkout Deployment is mid-rollout from ReplicaSet revision 41 to 42 and is banded by revision: six Degraded rev 42 blocks with an accent outline on top of four muted rev 41 blocks, labelled rollout 6/10 with maxSurge 25 %, and above it a wireframe HPA envelope of ghost blocks up to 16 replicas at CPU 82 % against a 70 % target. The StatefulSet pg-orders shows ordinal blocks 0, 1 and 2 with dotted PVC anchor lines to volume discs under the plateau. The DaemonSets node-exporter and otel-agent are thin ribbons of tiny blocks along every node row. The CronJob nightly-reindex is a run of fading translucent blocks. Three Pending pods hover above payments in an Unscheduled cloud (0/42 nodes: Insufficient memory), one payments-api pod is Failing in CrashLoopBackOff after 14 OOMKilled restarts, and the Service payments-api is an arch gate with zero ready endpoints. An Ingress and a Gateway arc into ready checkout and catalog replicas. The managed control plane stands as a city hall at the plateau edge: apiserver, etcd and controller-manager OK, scheduler Watch on latency. Below the plateau the node floor is ghosted with runs-on threads from checkout blocks to their nodes. Docked 2D panels on the right follow the selected checkout Deployment: rollout ready versus desired per revision with the 12:19 config-change marker, restarts and OOM kills, and the Kubernetes event list from 12:19 to 12:31. Six numbered callouts explain the encoding.
